paper_id: Zhou et al. - 2015 - On Multipath Link Characterization and Adaptation for Device-Free Human Detection
title: On Multipath Link Characterization and Adaptation for Device-Free Human Detection
motivation: Multipath propagation deteriorates detection rates and shrinks coverage in indoor device-free sensing; existing work avoids multipath at the cost of coverage
problem_framing: How to characterize detection sensitivity via measurable metrics on commodity WiFi, and how to exploit reflected paths for wider coverage
key_insight: Multipath factor μ—ratio of LOS power to total power—serves as a directly measurable runtime proxy for link sensitivity, enabling subcarrier weighting to boost detection
method_signature: Subcarrier + path weighting scheme using multipath factor μ and MUSIC angle-of-arrival
evaluation_criteria: True Positive rate vs False Positive rate (ROC curves); detection range at 90% minimal detection rate
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Path weighting causes slight performance drop in some cases due to angle estimation errors >20 degrees with only 3 antennas
evidence_for_taste: motivates us to take a deeper analysis
thinking_moves: 将传统上被视为干扰的多径重新诠释为可利用的资源
从物理建模出发推导可测量的代理指标(multipath factor)
利用OFDM子载波的频率分集实现灵敏度可调
借助MUSIC算法和多天线实现空间分集以区分LOS与反射路径
